items.title: The preamble of §15.1: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$

book.label: §15.1, preamble, p. 683 (2017: §15.1)
book.statement: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ is the set of finite formal sums with coefficients in $\mathbb Q^+$ of sc-Fredholm operators $T_xX \to W_x$, for smooth $x$; a morphism $\varphi$ acts by $\varphi_*$.

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.GrF x := (T_xX →ₗ[ℝ] W_x) →₀ ℚ≥0` for $x \in X_1$, with $W_x = P^{-1}(x)$ and $T_xX$ the project's tangent fibre; the chart version `Linearization15.GrFModel`.

diff: Formal sums are finitely supported functions, defined at all level-1 points. That the summands are sc-Fredholm is not part of the type; it is proved for the summands that occur (V15.9, gap G.145 closed); $\varphi_*$ and $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$ as a category are not built (gap G.144).

items.title: Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1), the linearization $T(f,\Lambda)$ is well defined

book.label: §15.1, Theorem 15.1.1, pp. 684–687 (2017: Theorem 15.1)
book.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ there is a unique section functor $T(f,\Lambda)$ of $\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X_\infty$ with (1) $T(f,\Lambda)(x) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ and (2) $T(f,\Lambda)(y) = \sum_{f(y) = s_i(y)} \sigma_i (f - s_i)'(y)$ for any local sc⁺-section structure.

lean.statement: `theorem_15_1_1_intrinsic`: for `A.E.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f`, two local section structures `IsLocalRepOn A Λ O s σ`, `IsLocalRepOn A Λ O′ t τ` on open sets and compatible charts with domains inside them, `linSumIntr c hx f s σ = linSumIntr c′ hx′ f t τ` at every $x \in X_1$ in both charts ($\sum_{f(x) = s_i(x)} \sigma_i\,\Phi_x^{-1} \circ D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(\varphi x) \circ T\varphi$ in $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$). Chart form `theorem_15_1_1`, model form `theorem_15_1_1_model`. The value: `linearization_eq` (property (2) for any data), `nonempty_localLinData`; property (1): `linearization_eq_zero`.

diff: The well-definedness, the substance of the proof, is proved in a stronger form: at all level-1 points, for $\Lambda$ not necessarily a functor, using only sc-smoothness of $f$. Narrower because the functor property $T(f,\Lambda)(t\varphi) = \varphi_* T(f,\Lambda)(s\varphi)$ (gap G.144) is not formalized; the sc-Fredholm property of the summands is proved in the chart reading for $f$ with tame germ data (`linearization_summand_isScFredholm`, V15.9; gap G.145 closed).

Readings (Findings, Chapter 15, items 1, 2): (a) the separation argument runs in the level-1 topology, and the "weak topology" of the limit of derivatives is read as pointwise convergence on $E_0$ (the derivatives $D(g \circ r)$ of an sc¹ map are continuous only from level 1); (b) in the final display, presumably the sum is over $\{i : f(0) = s_i(0)\}$, since $f(0) = s_i(0)$ need not hold for all $i$; the proof compares the formal sums of pairs $(s_i(r(y)), D((f - s_i) \circ r)(y))$. "Without loss of generality $X = O$" is the chart change `toIntr_chart_independent`.

items.title: Remark 15.1.2 (2017: 15.1), (1) follows from (2)

book.label: §15.1, Remark 15.1.2, p. 684 (2017: Remark 15.1)
book.statement: $(f - s_i)'(y)$ is not defined unless $f(y) = s_i(y)$, but then it is not counted; with the empty sum $0$, (1) follows from (2).

lean.statement: `SBLocalization.linearization_eq_zero`: if $\Lambda(f(x)) = 0$ then `linearization f Λ x = 0`; chart forms `remark_15_1_2`, `remark_15_1_2_model`; with positive weights an operator lies in the support iff some $i$ with $s_i(y) = f(y)$ produces it (`mem_support_linSumModel_iff`).

diff: In Lean $(f - s_i)'$ is defined for every $i$ and the sum is filtered by $s_i(y) = f(y)$; (1) is derived from positivity of the weights and the count formula.

items.title: Proposition 15.1.3 (2017: 15.1), separating sequences

book.label: §15.1, Proposition 15.1.3, p. 684 (2017: Proposition 15.1)
book.statement: In the local model there are $x_k \to 0$ with $x_k \ne 0$ and a partition $I = I_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup I_p$ such that $s_i(x_k) = s_{i'}(x_k)$ iff $i, i'$ lie in the same $I_e$, and then $s_i = s_{i'}$ near $x_k$.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp`: in a first countable $T_1$ space $Z$, for finitely many maps continuous on an open $V \ni x_0$ with values in a Hausdorff space, and **$x_0$ not isolated** (`(𝓝[≠] x₀).NeBot`): $x_k \in V$, $x_k \ne x_0$, $x_k \to x_0$, and one partition $e : I \to \mathrm{Fin}\,p$ with `IsSeparatedAt s e (x k)` for all $k$. At an isolated point no such sequence exists: `not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`, `not_proposition_15_1_3_point` (a one-point model). Witness: `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness` ($\mathbb R$ at 0).

diff: Hidden hypotheses: $x_0$ is not isolated; witness `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness`.

At an isolated point of the local model (for instance a zero-dimensional $X$) a sequence $x_k \ne 0$, $x_k \to 0$ cannot exist, so the proposition does not hold as we read it there (`not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`); a degenerate case (Findings, Chapter 15, item 3). Theorem 15.1.1 is unaffected: its core lemma handles isolated points through locality. Otherwise the statement is more general: topological, with no sc-structure.

items.title: Lemma 15.1.4 (2017: 15.1), finite closed covers of a ball

book.label: §15.1, Lemma 15.1.4, p. 685 (2017: Lemma 15.1)
book.statement: If a ball $B_\varepsilon(y)$ in $\mathcal O$ (metric of $E_0$) is a finite union of sets closed in the ball, one of them has nonempty interior.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.lemma_15_1_4`, in any pseudo-metric space: for finitely many relatively closed $A_i$ with $\bigcup A_i = B_\varepsilon(y)$, some $A_i$ has nonempty interior; topological core `exists_nonempty_interior_of_finite_closed_cover`.

diff: The proof is by induction on the index set instead of moving $z$ step by step; it is applied on the level-1 topology (reading (a) of V15.2).

items.title: Lemma 15.1.5 (2017: 15.2), local dichotomy of finitely many sections

book.label: §15.1, Lemma 15.1.5, p. 685 (2017: Lemma 15.2)
book.statement: For $y$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $z$ with $d(z,y) < \varepsilon$, $\delta > 0$ and a partition $I_1, \dots, I_p$ with $B_\delta(z) \subset B_\varepsilon(y)$, $s_i = s_{i'}$ on $B_\delta(z)$ within one piece and $s_i \ne s_j$ pointwise on $B_\delta(z)$ across pieces.

lean.statement: `Linearization15.lemma_15_1_5`: in a pseudo-metric space, for finitely many maps continuous on $B_\varepsilon(y)$ into a Hausdorff space, exactly these conclusions, the partition a surjection $e : I \to \mathrm{Fin}\,p$; topological form `exists_isOpen_dichotomy`.

diff: The maps need only be continuous with values in a Hausdorff space; the sections need not be sc⁺.

book.label: §15.2, Definition 15.2.1, p. 688 (2017: Definition 15.2)
book.statement: (1) $(f,\Lambda)$ is transversal if at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$, $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ is a nonzero combination of surjective sc-Fredholm operators: all $(f - s_i)'(x)$ with $f(x) = s_i(x)$ are onto. items.title: Definition 15.3.1 (2017: 15.4), $(N,U)$ controls compactness

book.label: §15.3, Definition 15.3.1, p. 691 (2017: Definition 15.4)
book.statement: $(N,U)$ controls the compactness of $f$ if $U$ is a saturated open neighbourhood of $S_f$ and $\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$ has an orbit space with compact closure in $|X|$. Paracompact $|X|$ is a standing hypothesis, and $N : W \to [0,\infty]$.

lean.statement: `ControlsCompactness A f N U := A.E.IsAuxNorm N ∧ IsOpen U ∧ A.X.IsSaturated U ∧ solutionSet A.P f ⊆ U ∧ IsCompact (closure (A.X.π '' {x ∈ U | A.B.AuxLe N (f x) 1}))`; `ControlsCompactness.mono` (a smaller saturated open $U' \supseteq S_f$).

diff: $N$ is defined on $W_{0,1}$ (Definition 12.2.1 = 8.3.5); "$N(f(x)) \le 1$" is `AuxLe` ($f(x) \in W_{0,1}$ and $N \le 1$), the text's $+\infty$ extension on p. 691. Paracompactness of $|X|$ is not part of the definition, which makes it more general; theorems that need it carry it.

items.title: Definition 15.3.3 (2017: 15.5), $(N,U)$-admissible perturbations

book.label: §15.3, Definition 15.3.3, p. 692 (2017: Definition 15.5)
book.statement: An $(N,U)$-admissible perturbation is an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ with $N(\Lambda)(x) \le 1$ for all $x$ and $\{x \mid \exists t \in [-1,1],\ (t\Lambda)(f(x)) > 0\} \subseteq U$.

lean.statement: `IsAdmissible A f N U Λ := IsScPlusMultisection A Λ ∧ (∀ x, pointwiseNorm N Λ x ≤ 1) ∧ {x | ∃ t ∈ Icc (-1:ℝ) 1, 0 < multisectionSmul t Λ (f x)} ⊆ U`.

diff: The text's standing data ($f$ sc-Fredholm, $|S_f|$ compact, $(N,U)$ controlling compactness) are hypotheses of the theorems that use the predicate. $t\Lambda$ is `multisectionSmul` (Definition 13.2.10) and $N(\Lambda)$ is `pointwiseNorm` (Definition 13.2.3).

items.title: Definition 15.3.5 (2017: 15.6), general position

book.label: §15.3, Definition 15.3.5, p. 693 (2017: Definition 15.6)
book.statement: $(f,\Lambda)$ is in general position if for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ every $L_i$ of $T(f,\Lambda)(x) = \sum \sigma_i L_i$ is surjective on $T^R_xX$; the reduced linearization is $T^R_{(f,\Lambda)}(x)$.

lean.statement: `IsInGeneralPosition A f Λ`: for all `x : A.X.PObj.Level 1` with `0 < Λ (f x)` and all `L ∈ (linearization f Λ x).support`, `L.domRestrict (reducedTangentFiber hφ hx T)` is surjective, for every chart $\varphi$ around $x$ and presentation $T$ of its partial quadrant. `exists_chart_presentation`; `isInGeneralPosition_iff_exists` (one chart and presentation per point suffices); `reducedLinearization f Λ x φ T` and `isInGeneralPosition_iff_reducedLinearization`; `mem_levelSet_one_of_pos` ($\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f) \subseteq X_1$); witness `isInGeneralPosition_witness n` (on `epSEP n 0`, the zero section with $\Lambda_0$, support everything).

diff: The point is taken in `Level 1`, where `linearization` lives; `mem_levelSet_one_of_pos` shows nothing is lost. "Every chart" reads $T^R_xX$ chart-wise (Part I's `reducedTangentFiber`); since that space is chart independent, `isInGeneralPosition_iff_exists` gives the "some chart" form; the all-charts form is satisfiable (`isInGeneralPosition_witness`). Tameness of $X$ is not assumed in the definition; it is needed only for $T^R_xX$ to be the right space.

items.title: Remark 15.3.6 (2017: 15.6), first sentence: general position gives surjectivity

book.label: §15.3, Remark 15.3.6, first sentence, p. 693 (2017: Remark 15.6)
book.statement: In general position, $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ is onto for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$.

lean.statement: `IsInGeneralPosition.surjective`: every operator of the support of `linearization f Λ x` is surjective.

diff: "Onto" is read operator by operator, as in Definition 15.3.5. The rest of the remark (good position at $\partial X$, tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoid) is gap G.161.

items.title: Corollary 15.3.10 (2) (2017: 15.1 (2)), an auxiliary norm on $[0,1] \times X$ controlling compactness

book.label: §15.3, Corollary 15.3.10 (2), p. 699, and the first step of its proof, pp. 699–700 (2017: Corollary 15.1 (2))
book.statement: Given regular perturbations $(N^i, U^i, \Lambda^i)$, $i = 0, 1$, there are an auxiliary norm $\widetilde N$ on $\widetilde W$ and a saturated open $\widetilde U \supseteq S_{\tilde f}$, restricting to $(N^i, U^i)$ over $i = 0, 1$, such that $(\widetilde N, \widetilde U)$ controls the compactness of $\tilde f$. The proof pulls one $N$ back to $\widetilde W$ with $\widetilde U = [0,1] \times U$.

lean.statement: The proof's step: `SEP.cubeAuxNorm n N` ($\widetilde N(q,x,h) = N(h)$, Part I's `pullbackAuxNorm`), `isAuxNorm_cubeAuxNorm` (an auxiliary norm of $(\widetilde W, \tilde\mu)$, invariant under $\tilde\mu$), `controlsCompactness_cube` (if $(N,U)$ controls the compactness of $f$, then $(\widetilde N, [0,1]^n \times U)$ controls that of $\tilde f$). The statement: `interpAuxNorm A N₀ N₁` $= \max(\alpha(t)N^0, \beta(t)N^1)$ with $\alpha = \min(1, 3(1-t))$, $\beta = \min(1, 3t)$, `interpSet A U₀ U₁` $= ([0,2/3) \times U^0) \cup ((1/3,1] \times U^1)$, and `corollary_15_3_10_2 (hf) (h₀ : ControlsCompactness A f N₀ U₀) (h₁ : … N₁ U₁) : ControlsCompactness (A.cubeSEP 1) (cubeLiftEp f hf) (interpAuxNorm A N₀ N₁) (interpSet A U₀ U₁)`, with the restrictions `interpAuxNorm_of_cubeTime_eq_zero`, `_eq_one`, `mem_interpSet_zero`, `mem_interpSet_one`.

diff: The text does not give $\widetilde N$; its proof uses a single $N$; both forms are proved. The $\Lambda^i$ play no role in (2). That $\tilde f$ is sc-Fredholm carries Part I's tame germ data (V15.18). Parts (1) and (3) of the corollary are gap G.162.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 15.1.1, the functor property of $T(f,\Lambda)$
notFormalized.label: §15.1, Theorem 15.1.1, p. 684 (2017: Theorem 15.1)
notFormalized.book: For a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ between smooth points, $T(f,\Lambda)(y) = \varphi_* T(f,\Lambda)(x)$, where $\varphi_*$ maps $\sum \sigma_i L_i$ to $\sum \sigma_i\,\mu(\varphi,\cdot) \circ L_i \circ T\varphi^{-1}$.
notFormalized.instead: What exists: $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ at every $x \in X_1$ (`SBLocalization.linearization`, `linearization_eq`; V15.2, V15.8); the summands and `toIntr`, with the sc-Fredholm property of the summands (`linearization_summand_isScFredholm`, V15.9); wave 1's machinery for morphisms in Part I's `ChartPoint` picture: `EpStrongBundle.morIso` (the local strong bundle isomorphism of the sheet of $\varphi$), `LocalIso.pullPt`, `morTx`/`morKx` for $T\varphi$ and $\mu(\varphi,\cdot)$, `lemma_12_5_1_*`. Missing: (i) $\varphi_*$ on `GrF` (`Finsupp.mapDomain` of $L \mapsto \mu(\varphi,\cdot) \circ L \circ T\varphi^{-1}$), about 40 lines; (ii) the transport of a local section structure along $t \circ s^{-1}$ near $\varphi$ ($\mu \circ s_i \circ (ts^{-1})^{-1}$ is sc⁺ and represents $\Lambda$ near $y$ by `IsWFunctor`), about 120 lines; (iii) a bridge from `toIntr`/`subDeriv` to `morTx`/`morKx` and the chain rule for $D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)$ under the local strong bundle isomorphism, about 200–300 lines. Estimate 350–500 lines.

notFormalized.title: §15.1 and Theorem 15.1.1 (2): the summands of $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ are sc-Fredholm
notFormalized.label: §15.1, preamble and Theorem 15.1.1 (2), pp. 683–684 (2017: §15.1, Theorem 15.1)
notFormalized.book: Each $(f - s_i)'(x)$ with $f(x) = s_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm operator $T_xX \to W_x$, so $T(f,\Lambda)(x) \in \mathrm{GrF}(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-13, Part III wave 2; V15.9; `Chapter15/P3L_FredholmSummands.lean`), in the chart reading and with Part I's inherited tame germ data. For $f$ with `IsScFredholmSectionTame`, $s_i$ sc⁺ on $O$ and $f(x) = s_i(x)$, the chart operator $D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(z)$ of $(f - s_i)'(x)$ restricts to an sc-Fredholm operator $T_zO \to K_z$, Fredholm on every level with constant index (`subDeriv_isScFredholm`, from Part I's `StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm` for $(f - s_i)|_O$ on $W|_O$); every operator in the support of $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ is such a $(f - s_i)'(x)$ (`linearization_summand_isScFredholm`). $T_xX$ and $W_x$ carry no sc-structure in the project, so the property is read in the chart; `GrF` is not cut down to a subtype.

notFormalized.title: Tame solution sets and tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoids in §15.2

notFormalized.title: The ep-groupoid $U(x)$ of Remark 15.2.3
notFormalized.label: §15.2, Remark 15.2.3, p. 689 (2017: Remark 15.2)
notFormalized.book: On the ep-groupoid $U(x)$ the functor $z \mapsto \Lambda(f(z))$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid.
notFormalized.instead: The local branching structure is given on $X$ at the support points of $U(x)$ (`remark_15_2_3_hyp`, V15.13). The restriction of the ep-groupoid to the $G_x$-invariant open $U(x)$ is not built; it is not needed for §§15.3–15.5 as far as we can see. About 80 lines.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 15.4.1 and Definition 15.4.2: the canonical oriented lift $\hat T_{(\Lambda \circ f, o)}$
notFormalized.label: §15.4, Theorem 15.4.1, Definition 15.4.2 (2017: Theorem 15.6, Definition 15.7)
notFormalized.book: Under Assumption 15.4, for an oriented sc⁺-Fredholm section functor $(f,o)$ and an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$, the tangent functor $T_{(f,\Lambda)}$ has a canonical lift to formal sums of oriented sc-Fredholm operators, given in a local sc⁺-section structure by $\sum \sigma_i \cdot (\ker(f - s_i)'(y), o_{i,y})$.
notFormalized.instead: Not formalized. It needs: the category $\widehat{Gr}_F(X)$ of finite formal sums of oriented sc-Fredholm operators and its forgetful functor to $Gr_F(X)$ (about 250 lines); the orientation of $(f - s)'(y)$ induced by $o$, through Part I's `orTransfer` between linearizations of $f - s$ for different $s$ (about 200 lines); independence of the local sc⁺-section structure (about 300 lines, on top of the $T_{(f,\Lambda)}$ interface, gap G.144); continuity of $o_{i,y}$ along $M_i$ (needs G.138, about 300 lines). The transport of orientations along equivalences is `orEqv`, `pushOr` (V12.39). Estimate 1,000 lines after G.138.

notFormalized.title: Product strong bundles and product multisections
notFormalized.label: §15.3, the remark after Definition 15.3.3 and Remark 15.3.4, pp. 692–693 (2017: Remark 15.5)
notFormalized.book: $W \times W' \to X \times X'$ with $\mu \times \mu'$, $f \times f'$, $N \times N' = \max$, and $\Lambda \times \Lambda'$ an sc⁺-multisection; admissibility is preserved, and the domain support lies in $(U \times X') \cup (X \times U')$.
notFormalized.instead: Only the ep-groupoid level exists (`EpGroupoid.prod`, V15.17). Part I has no product of strong bundles: a product strong-bundle atlas, the fibre $W_x \times W'_{x'}$ over $(x,x')$, and $\mu \times \mu'$ are missing, and so is the sc⁺ property of $\Lambda \times \Lambda'$. Estimate 500–1,000 lines (bundle 300–600; multisection and admissibility 200–400).

notFormalized.title: Remark 15.3.6 after its first sentence
notFormalized.label: §15.3, Remark 15.3.6, p. 693 (2017: Remark 15.6)
notFormalized.book: At $x \in \partial X$, general position gives good position; $\Lambda \circ f$ is a tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoid.
notFormalized.instead: Only the first sentence is formalized (`IsInGeneralPosition.surjective`, V15.25). The rest needs the step of gap G.151 (general position implies good position) and the tameness of gap G.150, on top of the local solution sets of §15.2 (V15.12–V15.15). Estimate 150–300 lines.

notFormalized.label: §15.3, Theorem 15.3.7, Theorem 15.3.9, Corollary 15.3.10 (1), (3), pp. 694–700 (2017: Theorems 15.4, 15.5, Corollary 15.1)
